nodes.description: External interface function init(uint numTokens, address target) declared in ReservoirLike; has no access control and can be invoked on any contract implementing the interface.
External interface function drip() declared in ReservoirLike; callable by anyone and mutates reservoir state in the implementing contract.

Unauthenticated payable fallback function of Proxy. It copies calldata into memory and unconditionally delegatecalls a hardcoded implementation address 0x9a2E280aAeB4dE82AAD34Df9c114f67A1699744c, propagating revert/return of the delegatecall.
Attacker-controlled external caller. Nothing in Proxy restricts who may invoke the fallback, and the caller's identity/context is preserved into the delegatecall.

Assembly delegatecall to a hardcoded target with fully attacker-controlled calldata. Executes arbitrary external code in the storage/context of Proxy, enabling arbitrary state manipulation and re-entrant callbacks.
Unsigned integer parameter of ReservoirLike.init controlling the number of tokens to initialise.
Address parameter of ReservoirLike.init used as the initialisation target; unvalidated attacker-supplied address.

edges.reason: Any external account (msg.sender) can invoke the payable fallback of Proxy; there is no owner check, whitelist or access modifier, so an arbitrary untrusted caller controls entry into the proxy.

The untrusted caller's identity and msg.data are preserved through delegatecall, letting an arbitrary msg.sender drive the unsafe delegatecall and execute privileged code in the proxy's storage context.
The fallback unconditionally executes delegatecall with the raw attacker-supplied calldata against the hardcoded implementation, achieving unrestricted arbitrary code execution.

External code reached through delegatecall executes inside the proxy and can call back into Proxy (or its implementation) before the current frame finishes, enabling re-entrant manipulation of the same storage.
The numTokens parameter is consumed as an argument of ReservoirLike.init.
The target parameter is consumed as an argument of ReservoirLike.init and is not validated before use.

normalization_plan.reason: numTokens is a non-core parameter that exists only as an input of the core init function; it carries no independent state and should be absorbed into ReservoirLike.init.
target is a non-core parameter used solely as the initialisation address of ReservoirLike.init; it should be folded into the core init function node.
